headline: Philippines Posts Highest PISA Scores Yet, but Learning Gaps Remain Large
seoTitle: Philippines Posts Highest PISA Scores Yet in 2025 | FMB News
seoDescription: The Philippines improved in science, mathematics and reading in PISA 2025, posting its highest scores since joining the assessment, but large learning gaps remain.
deck: Filipino 15-year-olds posted the country's strongest PISA results since the Philippines joined the assessment, with gains in science, mathematics and reading. The improvement is significant, but the scores still show a large share of learners struggling to meet baseline proficiency.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Philippines recorded its highest scores to date in the Programme for International Student Assessment after the OECD released the PISA 2025 results on September 8.

Philippine students averaged 373 points in science, 371 in mathematics and 367 in reading. Philstar reported that these were improvements of 17 points in science, 16 points in mathematics and 20 points in reading compared with the country's 2022 results. GMA News separately reported that the Philippines posted its highest-ever mean scores in all three subjects.

PISA measures how well 15-year-old students can apply knowledge and skills in real-world situations. More than 760,000 students in 91 countries and economies participated in the 2025 cycle, with science as the main assessment domain.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The Philippines first joined PISA in 2018 and has repeatedly ranked among the weakest-performing participating education systems. The 2025 improvement therefore marks a measurable change from the country's previous results rather than simply a change in ranking language.

The broader international picture was also difficult. The OECD said average performance across its member countries declined to the lowest levels observed in science, reading and mathematics, with especially steep declines in reading.

The OECD also highlighted new concerns around digital distraction, AI use and students' ability to evaluate information. These issues matter for the Philippines because learning recovery now involves not only basic literacy and numeracy but also digital and information literacy.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: The result is one of the clearest international measures of whether Philippine learning outcomes are moving in the right direction. Higher scores suggest that recent recovery efforts may be producing gains, but the country remains far from a point where strong foundational skills can be taken for granted.

Education performance affects more than schools. Weak reading, mathematics and science skills shape future employment, productivity, inequality and the country's ability to compete in higher-value industries. The new scores therefore matter to families, employers and economic planners as much as they do to educators.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: The next question is whether the gains can be sustained and translated into a larger share of students reaching baseline proficiency, especially in reading and mathematics.

Readers should watch for the Department of Education's detailed response to the 2025 results, any changes to learning-recovery programs, teacher support, digital access and curriculum implementation, and the OECD's country-level analysis of the Philippines as more detailed PISA material is released.

audit.socialCaption: The Philippines posted its highest PISA scores yet: 373 in science, 371 in mathematics and 367 in reading. The improvement is real, but the learning gap remains large. FMB News explains what changed and why the results matter beyond the classroom.
verificationNotes: The release date, scope and international methodology are verified from the OECD's PISA 2025 publication and program pages.
The Philippine scores and changes from 2022 are corroborated by Philstar and GMA News, which attribute the Philippine figures to the released PISA results and DepEd.
The article avoids presenting ranking language as the main finding because rank positions can shift with participating systems and do not by themselves measure learning improvement.
The story distinguishes measurable score gains from the continuing proficiency problem and does not imply that the Philippine learning crisis has been resolved.
Repository search found no existing FMB News article on PISA 2025 Philippines, so this is treated as an original report.
The hero and social crops are FMB-owned editorial graphics using the approved FMB icon and purple-violet/plum treatment and are explicitly not documentary photographs.
